title.narrative: Output 6.4. Increased capacity of ILO constituents to strengthen legislation, polices and measures to ensure equal opportunities and treatment in the world of work for persons with disabilities and other persons in vulnerable situations

description.narrative:
1. In 2020 the Ministry of Health and Child Care and the National AIDS Council (NAC) concluded implementation of a pilot programme for demand generation for SRHR and HIV services for artisanal miners at Venice Mine in Mhondoro-Ngezi:
a. The pilot promoted the uptake of HIV Self-testing services for artisanal miners, young people and sex workers: 10,000 people were reached; 415,000 condoms distributed; 2000 people tested for HIV and screened for tuberculosis and cervical cancer in collaborative efforts of civil society and the private sector actors. 50 persons with disabilities received targeted violence and harassment, SRHR and HIV services.
2. In 2020-2021 the Zimbabwe Private Sector HIV/AIDS and Wellness Board extended support and services to the informal economy as part of its roles to coordinate the private sector response to HIV/AIDS.
a. Informal economy associations (IEAs) have provided awareness and education programmes for their members and created demand for HIV services and testing. The Zimbabwe Network of People Living with HIV and Aids (ZNPP+) delivered awareness raising on HIV/AIDS and COVID-19 to over 100 people living with HIV in the informal economy in Chitungwiza.
b. IEAs now participate in the Council of IEAs on HIV and Aids convened under the NAC private sector response. Informal economy operators have received business development services as a strategy to reduce risky behaviour and exposure to HIV through economic empowerment.
3. In October 2021, the Zimbabwe Occupational Health Nurses Association (ZOHNA) has increased access to HIV testing services for workers in the private sector.
a. Twenty-one companies are now providing HIV testing services and ART services to over 40,000 workers.
b. 100 inspectors have increased capacities for workplace inspections on HIV/AIDS & OSH & Violence and Harassment as guided by Statutory Instrument (SI) 105 of 2014 on Labour (HIV & AIDS) Regulations & in line with R200 and C 1. The ILO provided in March 2020 financial and technical resources through Unified Budget, Results and Accountability Framework (UBRAF) country envelope resources for the comprehensive HIV, TB and SRH pilot program for artisanal miners in Venice Mine in Mhondoro-Ngezi(Kadoma). In June 2021 the ILO prov financial and technical resources for a baseline survey of the gaps in service provisioning for persons with disabilities and has developed an intervention programme of support.
2. The ILO also organised a series of training in March to April 2021 of trainers activities to create a network of ‘Champions' in various sub-sectors in the informal economy and geographic locations. The Champions are a conduit to communicate correct information on SRHR, HIV/AIDS and Gender equality – including GBV. The ILO provided financial and technical inputs towards the development of the capacity needs assessment study, as well as the activities to build the capacity of service providers in the informal economy.
3. In September 2021, the ILO provided financial and technical resources through Unified Budget, Results and Accountability Framework (UBRAF) country envelope resources for the pilot project; and provided technical support for the training of nurses and the labour inspectors

Output 6.3. Increased capacity of member States to develop gender-responsive legislation, policies and measures for a world of work free from violence and harassment

description.narrative:
Through the EU-funded Spotlight Initiative (SI), the Government, in consultation with social partners, took measures to develop gender-responsive policies and measures for a world of work free from violence and harassment in line with C190 and R206. Through the Zimbabwe Gender Commission, developed, in consultation with tripartite plus constituents, a National Strategy for the Elimination of Sexual Harassment and Gender-Based Violence in the Workplace in Zimbabwe (finalized and adopted in April 2021). The Public Service Commission (PSC) developed a Policy on Sexual Harassment for the Public Sector in line with C190 and R206 (validated by tripartite constituents in December 2020). Final adoption expected before end of 2021.
The Zimbabwe Congress of Trade Unions (ZCTU) took measures to raise awareness on C190. In particular, the ZCTU engaged in several C190 advocacy and awareness raising activities, which reached 57 private sector companies from 14 different sectors in 17 districts across the country.
Moreover, the ZCTU Women's Committee held a series of engagements with female Parliamentarians on violence and harassment against women in the workplace to popularise and seek consensus on the ratification of C190. This resulted in an increased understanding of the issues of violence and harassment at work by Parliamentarians.
Following consultation and endorsement by representative employers' organisations, 9 private companies were identified in different sectors (banking, hospitality, manufacturing and ICT). Taking advantage of the Model Workplace Programme developed within the SI, these companies were given training on how to prevent and protect from violence and harassment. They were also given support for the development of a workplace policy on violence and harassment, which has been adopted in all the targeted companies. As part of the SI, the ILO provided support to sensitisation activities for key stakeholders on C190 and R206. In particular, the ILO provided both financial and technical support for the development of the National Strategy, which was adopted by tripartite plus constituents in April 2021.
Through SI, the ILO conceived and developed the Model Workplace Programme for the implementation of C190 at the workplace level. This Model Programme consists of three components: 1. policy development; 2. education and training, and 3. identification and training of gender champions. The ILO used this Model to support companies to increase their knowledge on issues related to violence and harassment and on C190 and R206, as well as to develop their internal workplace policies on violence and harassment in line with relevant labour standards.
In addition, the ILO, through SI, also provided financial support to support the Zimbabwe Congress of Trade Unions' outreach and sensitization programmes, including on the ratification of C190.
